$comment: Generated from the live wire types (the TerminalHub rtc trait and the vocabularies its channels carry). Regenerate with `HORIZON_BLESS_WIRE_SCHEMA=1 cargo nextest run -p horizon-acp -p horizon-terminal-core wire_schema`; additive-vs-reshape classification of changes is scripts/check-wire-schema.sh (docs/remoc-adoption-design.md §4).

ClientHello.description:
The client half of the version negotiation, carried by the first rtc
call on every connection (the hub's `hello`).

ClipboardDestination.description:
Which OS clipboard buffer a [`TerminalUpdate::Clipboard`] targets.
`Clipboard` is the explicit-copy path (Cmd/Ctrl+C, OSC 52 writes);
`Primary` is the X11/Wayland middle-click-paste buffer, written
automatically as selection completes/updates (Linux convention -- select
= copy to primary). One update type with a destination discriminator,
rather than a second full clipboard pathway.

HandOverRefused.description: Why [`TerminalHub::hand_over`] left the terminals where they were.

HubError.description:
The hub's error vocabulary. One enum for every method: domain errors
and transport errors share it, per remoc's own rtc pattern (the
`From<rtc::CallError>` impl is what lets a lost connection surface as
an `Err` from any pending call).

oneOf.description:
`hello`: the peers' version ranges do not overlap. Feeds the same
auto-drain recovery as the JSONL era's `HandshakeRejected`.
`attach_terminal`: no live terminal session with that id.

`create_terminal`: the PTY spawn itself failed (bad shell,
permissions, or the bounded spawn retries were exhausted). What the
JSONL wire reported as a `TerminalUpdate::Error` on the update
stream is now the create call's own result.

Transport failure of the rtc call itself, carried as its rendered
message (`rtc::CallError` itself is not `Eq`/`JsonSchema`; nothing
programmatic branches on its inner structure). Constructed
client-side by the `From<rtc::CallError>` impl below — a server
never sends it.

Any method other than `hello`/`drain` was called before a
successful `hello` on this connection. `hello` is contractually the
first call (§3), and the daemon enforces it rather than trusting
the client: a rejected or skipped negotiation must not grant access
to the negotiated-behavior surface. (`drain` stays reachable — it
is the version-stable recovery path a rejected client legitimately
uses.) Appended additively for v10.1 of the artifact's history —
an older client never triggers it (it always hellos first).

ProgramBlockedOn.description: What a blocked program is waiting for (the protocol's `kind`).

oneOf.description: At rest, waiting for the next instruction.
Finished a piece of work the user has not looked at yet.
Cannot go on until the user does something.
Failed and stopped.

Rgb.description:
The wire schema's [`Rgb`]: a plain `{r, g, b}` u8 struct, kept in sync
with its serde shape.

TerminalAttachment.description:
What [`TerminalHub::create_terminal`]/[`TerminalHub::attach_terminal`]
hand back: the session's live channels. `events` carries the
terminal's state and the bytes after it to a client that asks
(`TerminalCommand::WantState`, `docs/terminal-stream-design.md`), and
what the session says of itself (title, bell, clipboard, exit, error);
`commands` carries what the client sends. There are no frames: a client
draws from a terminal of its own.

commands.$comment: remoc rch channel half: a chmux port reference on the wire; the x-channel-payload schema is what flows through it

events.$comment: remoc rch channel half: a chmux port reference on the wire; the x-channel-payload schema is what flows through it

TerminalColorScheme.description:
Crate-local mirror of the host's theme color roles (the shell's
`src/theme/`). This crate has no dependency on the shell's theme or its
UI toolkit at all (`docs/session-daemon-design.md` decision 9), so
the host converts its live theme into this plain-data struct and pushes
it in via `TerminalCore::set_color_scheme` — the same "crate-local
newtype / plain-data mirror" pattern `crates/horizon-agent` already uses
for `SessionId`.

[`Default`] duplicates the host's own built-in theme defaults
(`ui::theme`'s `ansi` module and `text_primary`/`surface_base`/`accent`
roles) so a freshly constructed `TerminalCore` that never receives an
explicit scheme (every test in this crate) still answers color queries
with the same values Horizon has always shipped. In the running app this
default is only ever transiently observed (`TerminalSession::spawn`
pushes the live theme immediately after construction).

oneOf.description:
Bytes for the PTY: what a view's terminal wrote for a key, a paste,
a report to the program. The session loop writes them after what
the PTY has already said is answered (`docs/terminal-stream-design.md`).

Re-pushes the host's live theme-derived color scheme into a
*running* session's `TerminalCore` (`TerminalCore::set_color_scheme`),
so a subsequent OSC 10/11/12 query reply reflects a live theme apply
(`Reload Config` / the theme settings view) instead of the stale
spawn-time snapshot (`TerminalSpawnSpec::color_scheme`). App-set
live overrides (an OSC 4/10/11/12 write the attached app made
itself) still win over this, exactly as they do over the spawn-time
scheme: the engine answers from its palette, and the scheme is its
default palette (`TerminalCore::set_color_scheme`).

Client → daemon: a view is here and has nothing: the
terminal's state, then what the PTY writes from there on.

Client → daemon: no view is here any more: nothing of the
state or the PTY's bytes is to be sent until one asks again.

Client → daemon: this many bytes of `Output` have been
taken in. The daemon holds what it sends against these: a view that
falls too far behind is sent no more until it has caught up, and
then the state again.

TerminalHubHello.description:
`horizon-terminald`'s `hello` reply. Channel-free: the terminal domain's
only streams are per-attachment ([`TerminalAttachment`]).

`binary_id` is load-bearing beyond diagnostics here — it is the terminald
connection's skew insurance (`docs/terminald-split-design.md` decision
6). A terminald that outlives many UI rebuilds may be running an older
binary than the client that connects to it, and the layer *below* the
negotiated version (remoc/chmux framing, the Postbag codec) is not
covered by version negotiation at all — the tmux 3.6 lesson. The client
records this id at `hello` and names it if a post-`hello` decode failure
suggests exactly that kind of skew, so the failure surfaces as a clean
refusal pointing at `Reload Terminal Runtime` rather than as silent
misbehavior.

TerminalNotification.description:
A desktop-notification request a terminal app posted through the PTY
stream — OSC 9 (iTerm2-style: body only) or OSC 777 `notify`
(rxvt-style: optional summary + body). Extracted from the raw bytes
before the engine sees them (`core::osc_notify`) and delivered to the
client as [`TerminalUpdate::Notification`].

body.description: The message body (OSC 9's whole payload, OSC 777's second argument).

title.description:
The summary line (OSC 777's `notify ; <title> ; <body>` first
argument); `None` for OSC 9, which carries only a body.

TerminalProgramStatus.description:
What a program in the terminal says of its own state, read from the
root record of its OSC 7501 reports (the Program Status Protocol,
`core::program_status`) and delivered to the client as
[`TerminalUpdate::ProgramStatus`].

app.description: The program's name for itself, such as `claude-code`.

blocked_on.description:
What the program waits for. Only with [`ProgramState::Blocked`],
and not always then.

message.description: Why, or what about, in the program's words.

pixel_height.description: Grid height in pixels (`rows * line_height`); see `pixel_width`.

pixel_width.description:
Grid width in pixels (`cols * cell_width`), forwarded to the PTY's
`ws_xpixel` field so every process reading `TIOCGWINSZ` — not just
Horizon's own renderer — sees real geometry instead of zeros. Derived
in the host's terminal view (`src/terminal/mod.rs`) from measured
font metrics; `0` means "not yet known" (e.g. before the view has
laid out once).

TerminalUpdate.description:
What the daemon sends a client, on the attachment's `events` mpsc
channel (`TerminalAttachment::events`): the terminal's state and the
bytes after it, to a client that asked (`docs/terminal-stream-design.md`),
and what the session says of itself.

oneOf.description:
Daemon → client: a desktop-notification request (OSC 9 / OSC 777
`notify`) a terminal app posted — see [`TerminalNotification`].
Whether it actually surfaces is the client's call: Horizon escalates
to the OS notification center only when the session isn't already
the focused pane of the focused window.

Daemon → client: the terminal's whole state, as its engine
writes it out, in pieces: the last has `more` false. What follows is
the PTY's bytes from that state on.

Daemon → client: what the PTY wrote, as the daemon's own
terminal took it in.

Daemon → client: the terminal was resized here, between
the bytes before and the bytes after.

Daemon → client: the daemon's clock let a synchronized
update's hold go here, the program never having let it go. No byte
says so: a view's terminal lets its own hold go at this place in
the stream, and keeps no clock of its own.

Daemon → client: the session's current working directory, read from
its shell process (board #69). Sent when the value changes and once to
every newly installed subscriber, so a reattaching client learns the
current value without a request (`docs/terminald-split-design.md`).

Daemon → client: what the program in the session says of its own
state ([`TerminalProgramStatus`]), or `None` once it has taken its
report back, as one does on its way out. Sent when it changes and,
while there is one, once to every newly installed subscriber, as
the working directory is.

VersionRange.description:
An inclusive protocol-version range one peer supports, as exchanged in
a hub's `hello`.
